items.text: Hello, Park Managers!
[p align="start"]Today, 21 October, marks a very special occasion - Jurassic World Evolution 3 is officially one year old! And, of course, that calls for a celebration.

[p align="start"]Today we’re kicking things off with Free Update 1.5.5 (patch notes below), bringing Pentaceratops and Crichtonsaurus to the game as full family units. Even better, our remaining monthly updates will now feature two free returning base game Jurassic World Evolution 2 species instead of one.

[p align="start"]It’s been a packed year of content and we’re not done yet! Our second Jurassic World Evolution 3 Expansion arrives in early December. In this Expansion you’ll rejoin DIN, building sanctuaries around the equator with one vital goal: save prehistoric animals from a world and climate they never evolved for. We’ll have much more to share as launch gets closer!
[p align="start"]The Expansion will launch alongside a free update featuring the Nigersaurus and Tylosaurus…and yes, the Tylosaurus is going to have something to smile about.
[p align="start"]We hope you'll join us in celebrating all things Jurassic World Evolution 3, and feel free to share some of your favourite memories playing in the comments.
Introduced two new family units to the game - Crichtonsaurus & Pentaceratops.
Dinosaurs
Hybrids and Mutants no longer display a nest preference when placing a small land nest.
A range of cohabitation preferences have been updated to ensure species mutually like and dislike each other, where expected.
Yangchuanosaurus' jaw no longer overcloses when performing a Fight Struggle animation.
Resolved an issue whereby 100% genome was not obtainable for some species in select Challenge levels.
Species with the 'Loner' trait have had their feeder requirements greatly reduced in comparison to those without this trait.
Frontier Workshop
Resolved an issue where some players would fail to connect to Frontier Workshop.
Stability & Performance
General performance and stability improvements
If you encounter any issues whilst playing Jurassic World Evolution 3, please report them on our dedicated Issue Tracker site.
For any support queries, you can reach out to our team using this form.

A new era is born! Jurassic World Evolution 3: Rebirth Expansion is available now on PC and Console.

Inspired by the events of Jurassic World Rebirth, unleash 4 movie themed species, experience a full narrative campaign inspired by Jurassic World: Rebirth and enhance your locations with a range of detailed scenery pieces!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/91636497ce1afcada9400f7441639414a72a4efe.jpg"]The Distortus rex is the first of its kind with unique kill animations and immense aggression. Challenge your facility’s security against a relentless dinosaur that puts staff safety to the ultimate test.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/b363ea6b1c9b18ed2aad5b477a6b9bcec9c641a6.jpg"]

The Mutadon is a versatile species, able to traverse both land and air with equal ferocity! Combining the cunning hunting abilities of the Velociraptor with the Pterosaur’s dominance of the air, this calculated predator poses a serious challenge to contain.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/08df721cd7c8838769cc3ea98e0d07ec20fdfac9.jpg"]Where does the dinosaur begin and the tail end? The Titanosaurus family unit have pillar like legs to hold its incredible weight and a long, slender tail. Towering over Île Saint-Hubert, uncover the iconic species from the movie with the never-before-seen juvenile variant.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/17233e6532c7ef2fda1e8d15970a1f8ca2d81406.jpg"]

Small in size but huge in appeal, the Aquilops family unit brings variety to the ceratopsian roster. Featuring a unique striped tail, this little herbivore's name means 'Eagle Face', referring to its distinctive beak.
Learn even more about how the four new species of Jurassic World Rebirth were taken from the silver screen to your monitor with our Behind the Scenes article.

Inspired by the events of Jurassic World Rebirth, push the boundaries of science and develop a top-secret facility across three stunning locations. Use new technology to manage formidable predators, study enormous dinosaurs and synthesise semi-aquatic wonders as a part of the team on Île Saint-Hubert.
Dive into our Behind the Scenes to look at how our Development Team crafted the campaign for Jurassic World Evolution 3: Rebirth Expansion.
Science Expanding Features
Geothermal Power

Harness the power of Île Saint-Hubert with geothermal power! Build and carefully manage a vast network of underground pipes to ensure a steady distribution of power across your facility, keeping chaotic consequences at bay!
Experimental Traits
Jurassic World Evolution 3: Rebirth Expansion introduces new experimental traits to enhance your prehistoric species and push the boundaries of scientific research.
Open Air Aviaries
Bring your flying enclosures to all new heights with the Open Air Aviary with raised flying heights, no visual obstruction, and expanded terrain editing heights.

Enhance your parks with a host of new facility blueprints and scenery pieces from the Île Saint-Hubert campaign! Construct geothermal piping, structural gantries, and iconic buildings inspired by the movie.
Île Saint-Hubert boasts a rich history, offering a glimpse of the past events preceding the return of dinosaurs with mysterious Mayan architecture on the island.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/7f71c3354c5f765ca3ab678337b6105a8fc4370e.jpg"]Unlock more Jurassic World Rebirth movie inspired skins, adult model variants, extra colours and patterns to use with your existing species from the Jurassic World Evolution 3 base game.
Tyrannosaurus rex – 1 new model, 1 Jurassic World Rebirth movie skin, 12 skin colours, 6 patterns
Spinosaurus – 1 new model, 3 Jurassic World Rebirth movie skins, 12 skin colours, 6 patterns
Mosasaurus – 1 new model, 1 Jurassic World Rebirth movie skin, 12 skin colours, 6 patterns
Quetzalcoatlus – 1 new model, 1 Jurassic World Rebirth movie skin, 12 skin colours, 6 patterns
Dilophosaurus – 1 Jurassic World Rebirth movie skin
Velociraptor – 2 movie skins
You can’t run this facility on your own, equip your staff with new Jurassic World Rebirth themed skins for the SUV, MVU, ATV, and Helicopters.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/2910fa7a92d087101269ea42c6173438d89bcf18.jpg"]
Update 1.3 brings a plenty of brilliant updates and improvements, including the returning Cearadactylus, changes to Aviaries and Pterosaur & Tyrannosaurus rex behaviours.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/664cd95c91a6145221210df9e87852158e3d1c9c.jpg"]The Cearadatylus returns as a full family unit alongside Update 1.3! This pterosaur will be the ideal addition to your park alongside the new improvements to aviaries.

With it's long, thin beak and sharp teeth this piscivore dips down into the water to snag and eat fish. The Cearadactylus' name translates to 'Ceara's lethal finger', which is a reference to the location of it's discovery and its wicked talons.

Aviaries have been updated, with terrain editing restrictions being greatly relaxed. Pterosaurs can now navigate freely under, around or through scenery where space allows and two new custom perch points can be placed or added to scenery and blueprints, allowing flying species to perch almost anywhere.
Additionally, the Cretaceous Cruise can now pass through Aviaries, allowing your guests to observe flying species from the attraction.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/29172ad359181923cc220a6775aba7ca0ec25394.jpg"]
Tyrannosaurus rex adults are now able to swim through deep water.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/93c5f5edd9858b4c9f5d7f761dfd67c0f8659979.jpg"]
Ranger teams in 4x4s now have access to a handheld flare to lure or repel dinosaurs with. Carnivores and armoured herbivores will be drawn towards the flare, while other dinosaurs will run from it.

The land Hatchery now has a Drone, and a 'Deep Analyser' tool has been added to all Hatchery drones; Land, Lagoon, and Aviary. Using the Deep Analyser tool will reward you with cash and genome points when scanning species
You can now favourite scenery items for easy access at the top of their respective menus and Blueprints can now be filtered to help players find similar items.
A number of existing grid-based scenery walls have had non-grid versions added, alongside some new scenery pieces.
Scenery lighting now has the option to be turned on during the daytime.
Plus, a whole host of bug fixes and other improvements for the base-game.

It's time to unearth the Wetlands Pack in Jurassic World Evolution 3, available now on all platforms.
Featuring three stunning new dinosaurs, each with their own striking family unit and a selection of swampy scenery items for you to decorate your enclosures.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/d8ba63fca12fe1df96b8679f5e1795806fe941df.jpg"]
A fierce spinosaurid, the Irritator is an impressive semi-aquatic carnivore bound to wow your guests in their new waterside enclosures.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/48a637156c757d833622cfce6589b9f6b92275b9.jpg"]
Adept at catching fish in their fish feeders and seeking out prey on land, Austroraptor is a larger, versatile relative of the Velociraptor.
Hypsilophodon
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/3f8b7dd943aae54fa9b963352f782d5b12182399.jpg"]
Emerging in herds, the Hypsilophodon favours warm, swampy environments with plenty of vegetation for them to eat!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/42bfac30fabdff9214b69ca847b052101b91337b.jpg"]

Using the hundreds of new scenery pieces, create lush open environments filled with greenery for the Hypsilophodon to roam or build dense, humid swamps with abandoned jetties for the Irritator to swim and catch fish.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/afbbca6b7e624652460353716670f2814c43b36e.jpg"]
Quickly design misty waterside enclosures with the thirteen new blueprints, including a boathouse, rusty shacks and wooden pontoons, inspired by wetland and bayou locations.
Take a look at the Frontier Workshop to browse blueprints for your parks made by our amazing community.
That's not all - the Wetlands Pack launches alongside a free major update! Take a look at what's included below.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/1aac367330857d14135dc7fac228cec656ed790b.jpg"]

A fan favourite, this large semi-aquatic ornithomimosaur returns in Update 1.2 as a special gift! Arriving at your enclosures as a full family unit, the Deinocheirus has huge forelimbs with sharp claws, perfect for foraging for food and defending juveniles.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/a3a604a14fbaccb3391a4c85173a0dc5ddf42ba4.jpg"]
With its toothless duck-like bill and feathery tail, this late Cretaceous giant will be right at home in your existing parks, and your new Wetland enclosures.
This new environment brush for Temperate and Tropical biomes paints your enclosures with new Cypress Trees and introduces an atmospheric mist that seeps across the landscape.
Also included are a variety of Cypress Trees as scenery items for Park Managers who want to finesse the details of their parks.
Alongside the Tropical biome, the Island Generator now has three more biomes to choose from when starting their island customisation, including;
· Desert
· Mediterranean
· Temperate

A new Beaches slider has also been added to the mode, allowing Park Managers to adjust the prominence of sandy beaches or cliff faces on generated islands. Islands can now feature more cliffs or more beaches depending on your preferences!

The updates to the Island Generator don't stop there - There's now a greater flexibility in building across your generated islands. Players are now able to place buildings, paths, and edit terrain up to the water's edge, as well as decorate the area with scenery beyond the island boundaries. We can't wait to see what islands you create next!
A collision heatmap showing where all sizes of dinosaur can roam, as well as where your guests and vehicles can move around your park.
New Blueprints menu allows you to see your own custom blueprints and the creations you've downloaded from the Workshop.
Path Copy feature gives you the ability to quickly and simply match pathing options throughout your park.
Plus, there's a whole host of bug fixes and improvements in Update 1.2 as well.
Please refer to the Update Notes for a full list of what's included. To see the update in action take a look at our Highlight video!

Hello Park Managers,
Next week, we’ll be releasing Update 1.1 for Jurassic World Evolution 3, which contains our first new content alongside several key improvements.
Kentrosaurus Family Unit
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/27415a56ceef7bc9711fc4a5c766887ba497f74f.png"]

Update 1.1 will contain our first free returning base game dinosaur from Jurassic World Evolution 2, the Kentrosaurus, expanded to become a complete family unit. Featuring armour plates and spikes to intimidate predators, this herbivore co-habits particularly well with other families such as Sauropods and Ornithomimosaurids. More information about the Kentrosaurus will be available on the Dinosaur Database when the update goes live.

The remaining base game Jurassic World Evolution 2 species are currently ongoing development work, as we re-introduce these classic dinosaurs in Jurassic World Evolution 3 as complete family units, with dimorphism and juveniles.

We’re excited to announce that we will be introducing one base game species as complete family units from Jurassic World Evolution 2 every month starting from January 2026, we won’t charge you for these species.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649456/d62b576ffe94ba8febb56b94df060cba7f55fdd8.jpg"]

Since launch we’ve been excited to see how park managers have been using the new tools and features to bring their Jurassic World vision to life! The team has been hard at work to bring new updates, bug fixes, and stability improvements to the game and 1.1 is no different.
Ahead of 1.1 going live we wanted to share with you some of the changes coming in the patch.
Introduced a new family unit to the game - the Kentrosaurus
Adjusted navigation rules so that dinosaurs can travel beneath and around scenery items more freely
Added further keyboard shortcuts to in-game control hints when placing or moving scenery
Added 'Very High' setting to Foliage detail
Updated the 'Very High' quality preset to correctly use the 'Very High' settings for foliage and geo detail
Improved level of detail for feathered dinosaurs on lower spec hardware
Revised sandbox settings for preventing juveniles from being hunted in sandbox maps.
Path and Fence building modes now default 'Replace Mode' to 'Off' when opened
Pylons can now be placed between Islands on maps made with Island Generator
Added guest food scattering animation for Dinosaur Encounter attraction
Adjusted frequency of Dinosaurs present in Dinosaur Encounter attraction
Added group edit shortcut when playing with mouse. Double-click a group to enter group edit mode.
Added new help screens for Alternative Camera Controls and Foundation Floor Pieces
Added screen effect when time controls are open to clarify focus (gamepad only)
Created new biome filter label for foliage scenery items

Alongside the above updates, 1.1 has an extensive list of bug fixes and stability improvements to various areas of the game. A full changelog will be available on next week when 1.1 goes live on all platforms.
